## What was wrong

The inactive tension-only diagonal (M2, D→B) was deactivated by the solver, so its scalar `deflection('dy', …)` correctly returned `0`. But the sampled `deflection_array('dy', …)` returned nonzero, geometrically inconsistent values (e.g. `-3.564` at the j-end). Two root causes:

- `Member3D.D()` zeroed the axial (`DX`) nodal terms for inactive members while keeping DY/DZ/rotations, producing a partial displacement vector that transformed to geometrically wrong local deflections for non-axis-aligned members.
- The `*_array` result methods (shear, moment, torque, axial, deflection, rel_deflection) lacked the active-state guard that every scalar method already had, so they recovered results from that inconsistent vector instead of returning zero.

## The fix

`source/Pynite/Member3D.py`
- `D()` now always reads the full nodal displacement vector (removed the `if self.active[combo_name]` branch around `DX`). This is post-processing only — the solver uses the model's global displacement vector and skips inactive members during stiffness assembly, so analysis is unaffected.
- Added an inactive-member guard (`return vstack((x_array, zeros_like(x_array)))`) to all six `*_array` methods, mirroring the scalar methods' `return 0`.
- Imported `zeros_like`.

`source/Pynite/PhysMember.py`
- Added the same guard to all five overridden `*_array` methods (placed after `x_array` validation, before the sub-member loop). `rel_deflection_array` is inherited from `Member3D`, so it is covered automatically.
- Imported `vstack, zeros_like`.

The guard uses `self.active.get(combo_name, False)`, matching the existing `max_axial`/`min_axial` pattern, so it generalizes to any combo and never raises on missing keys. Because a physical member and all its sub-members are deactivated together, the check is correct for subdivided members and plain `Member3D` sub-members alike.

- Scalar vs. sampled forms now agree for all six result types, for both active and inactive members.
- Generalizes across load-sign reversal, compression-only elements, physical-member subdivisions (incl. plain `Member3D` sub-members), custom `x_array`, and the P-Delta post-processing path.
- Active-member force, bending, and second-order behavior is preserved: a results fingerprint (M0/M1 shear, moment, axial, deflection arrays; cantilever linear + P-Delta) is byte-identical to the baseline.
